hints.text: The small raised $3$ is not a multiplier. It tells you how many copies of $5$ to multiply together.
$5^3$ means $5 \times 5 \times 5$. Start with $5 \times 5 = 25$, then multiply that result by the last $5$.

explanation: The exponent counts the copies of the base, so $5^3 = 5 \times 5 \times 5$.
Multiply step by step: $5 \times 5 = 25$, and then $25 \times 5 = 125$.
So $5^3 = 125$. It is not $5 \times 3 = 15$, which is a common mistake.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture a cube
steps: 5³ counts the little blocks in a 5-by-5-by-5 cube.
One layer holds 5 × 5 = 25 blocks, and there are 5 layers: 25 × 5 = 125.
